newsitem.title: FINLAND: WAIT-AND-SEE POLICY ON EMU NOT JUSTIFIED - FINLAND.
newsitem.headline: WAIT-AND-SEE POLICY ON EMU NOT JUSTIFIED - FINLAND.

text.p: The Finnish government said on Thursday that a policy of wait-and-see on membership of the third stage of European economic and monetary union could not be justified.
"A policy of wait-and-see cannot be justified as contributing to the strengthening of the economy or as promoting convergence," the government said in a report to parliament.
"The costs of such a choice would probably exceed the benefits," it said.

Finland had two realistic alternatives regarding the coming single European currency: "participating in the Euro area among the first member states, or extending the convergence phase by participating in the new exchange rate system."

The third alternative proposed by a panel of economic experts, to live with a floating currency, would include "significant economic policy related constraints and problems," and was not in line with government policy, the report said.
"From the point of view of political influence, the government regards participation in the euro area to be favourable for the general objectives of Finnish-European policy," it said.

"The single currency area...would provide good conditions for accomplishing Finnish (economic) policy objectives during the following decades," it said adding, Finland would "most probably" demonstrate sufficient convergence for EMU membership in the first wave.
The government said it was well aware of the uncertainty factors related to the establishment and working of the single currency area.

"A survey of the alternatives indicates, however, that the uncertainties and risks in the other alternatives would probably be even greater than in participating in the euro area among the first member states."
Among the drawbacks of not joining EMU in the first group was that the Bank of Finland would not get a representative on the council of the European Central Bank, the government said.
"Remaining outside the euro area would prevent the Bank of Finland from participating in the decision-making on common monetary policy," it said

The government also said staying outside the first group "would imply giving up the cost savings obtainable from business transactions within the euro area, and remaining in the role of a bystander in the development of EMU".
Parliament will start debate on the report on May 20, but the legislators' final vote on Finnish EMU membership is not due until early 1998.
